pages.summary: A file opened for reading or writing, and closed.
body: `fopen` gives an identifier (3 or more; -1, with a message, when the file cannot be opened) for `fprintf`, `fgetl`, `fread` and the other low-level functions. The permission is `'r'` (read, the default), `'w'` (write, emptying the file), `'a'` (append), or with `'+'` both reading and writing; `'t'` or `'b'` asks for text or binary (the same here). `fclose` closes it (or every open file with `'all'`); files left open stay open until closed.
syntax: With a message when it fails.

pages.summary: Lines read one at a time, and the position in a file.
body: `fgetl` reads the next line without its line break, `fgets` with it; both give -1 at the end. `feof` says whether the end is reached, `ferror` the last error's message. `ftell` gives the position in bytes from the start, `fseek` moves it (from `'bof'`, `'cof'` or `'eof'`, the start, here or the end), and `frewind` goes back to the start.

pages.summary: Binary data read from a file and written to it.
body: `fwrite` writes the values of an array as bytes of a precision (`'uint8'` by default, or `'int16'`, `'double'`, `'float32'` and the like) and gives the count; `fread` reads them back, all of them or sizeA (a number, [m n] or [m Inf]), as doubles unless the precision says `'*int16'` (the same class) or `'int16=>single'`.

pages.summary: Formatted data read from files and text.
body: `fscanf` applies a format again and again to the file's text, gathering the numbers into a column (or sizeA). `textscan` reads columns: each conversion of the format is a column of the result, a cell array (numbers as numeric arrays, text as cells), with `'Delimiter'`, `'HeaderLines'`, `'CommentStyle'` and the like; it reads from a file or from text. `textread` is the older form, one output per field, from a file name.

examples.title: Numbers from text

pages.summary: Whole text files read and written.
body: `fileread` gives a file's whole text as one character vector; `readlines` gives its lines as a string column (without line breaks); `writelines` writes strings to a file, one per line (`'WriteMode'` `'append'` to add to it).

examples.title: A list kept in a file

pages.summary: Matrices and cell arrays read from delimited files and spreadsheets, and written.
body: `readmatrix` reads the numbers of a text file (or .xlsx spreadsheet), header lines detected or given, other cells NaN; `writematrix` writes a matrix comma-separated (or with `'Delimiter'`, or as a spreadsheet for .xlsx). `readcell` reads every cell, numbers and text, into a cell array, and `writecell` writes one.

examples.title: Numbers, and numbers with text

pages.summary: The older functions for numbers in delimited files.
body: `csvread` reads a comma-separated file of numbers, from a row and column offset (counting from 0); `dlmread` any delimiter. `csvwrite` and `dlmwrite` write them. `readmatrix` and `writematrix` are the newer forms.
